exercise.name: Cossack Squat

reference.title: Cossack Squat
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

exercise.laterality: Alternating sides (both sides in one loop)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as you sink to one side, breathe out as you rise through the middle.
breathing.cadence: About 1.6 s down, short pause, about 1.2 s up, per side

prescription.tempo: Slow and controlled, 1-2 s pause at the bottom
prescription.progression: Deeper range, longer pauses, then hold a light dumbbell at the chest (goblet).

cues.text: Very wide stance, toes turned out a little, arms reaching forward.
Breathe in and sit down over the right foot; the left leg straightens and its toes turn up onto the heel.
Right heel down, right knee over the toes, chest up; feel the stretch along the inner left thigh.
Breathe out and push back up through the middle; the left foot rolls back down flat.
Repeat to the left: sit over the left foot, the right leg straightens onto its heel.
Push back to the middle and stand tall.

mistakes.fix: Sit only as deep as the heel stays down; widen the stance a little.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to get lower
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest up and the arms forward as a counterweight.
Keep the knee over the toes.
Keep it long; let the foot turn up onto the heel.

kinematics.norm: Very wide, more than a side-lunge step; Riemann 2013 tested lateral steps of 60% of body height (clinical opinion for the cossack)
Deep, about 110-135 degrees at the bottom with the heel down (clinical opinion); deeper than a side lunge (Riemann 2013 reported side-lunge knee flexion about 13% lower than in forward lunges)
Knee straight, foot turned up onto the heel (reference movement; clinical opinion)
Large: the heel stays down as the knee travels forward (clinical opinion)
Leaning forward with a long back (clinical opinion)
Slow, about 1.5 s down with a short pause (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Riemann et al. 2013, biomechanical comparison of forward and lateral lunges at varying step lengths (J Sports Med Phys Fitness 53:130-138)
Escamilla et al. 2008, patellofemoral compressive force and stress during forward and side lunges with and without a stride (Clin Biomech 23:1026-1037)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Work in a range you can control; add load only once the bodyweight version is smooth.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Patellofemoral stress rises with knee flexion in side lunges (Escamilla 2008): stop short of pain.
modify: Knee or groin discomfort: shorter depth and a narrower stance.
Balance concerns: hold a post or the back of a chair in front.
regressions: Cossack squat to a box or with hands on a support.
progressions: Full depth with the heel down.
Goblet cossack squat with a light dumbbell.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Bent-leg knee extensors lower into and drive out of the deep side squat; knee and ankle impulses were greater in lateral than in forward lunges (Riemann 2013).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Bent-leg knee extensors lower into and drive out of the deep side squat; knee and ankle impulses were greater in lateral than in forward lunges (Riemann 2013).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Bent-leg hip extensor, working hardest out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Bent-leg hip extensor, working hardest out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Work on both sides: the bent leg controls the wide position and the straight leg is stretched along its inner thigh (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Work on both sides: the bent leg controls the wide position and the straight leg is stretched along its inner thigh (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension on the bent leg and lengthen on the straight leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension on the bent leg and lengthen on the straight leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Steadies the bent hip and keeps the knee over the foot (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Steadies the bent hip and keeps the knee over the foot (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Hold the bent-leg heel down as the knee travels forward; lateral lunges asked more of the ankle than forward lunges (Riemann 2013).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Hold the bent-leg heel down as the knee travels forward; lateral lunges asked more of the ankle than forward lunges (Riemann 2013).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk long while the hips shift side to side (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Control the shift from side to side (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Control the shift from side to side (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the chest up against the forward lean (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the chest up against the forward lean (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Hold the forward-leaning trunk and help lift out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Hold the forward-leaning trunk and help lift out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Hold the arms forward as a counterbalance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Hold the arms forward as a counterbalance (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Hips shift over the bent leg
